assessment.baseline: Every existing public command starts from a conservative Alpha assessment until command-specific evidence supports promotion.
assessment.history: Each immutable Git release tag snapshots this registry; branches are working lines and are not the historical source of truth.

planning.label: Planning
promotion_requirements: Accepted problem statement, intended users, and owner-visible outcome.
planning.summary: The capability has an accepted direction but is not presented as an executable QZX command.

proof_of_concept.label: Proof of concept
promotion_requirements: Isolated feasibility evidence and an explicit non-public scope.
proof_of_concept.summary: An isolated experiment is validating feasibility; it is not part of the public command contract.

alpha.label: Alpha
promotion_requirements: Public implementation with documented parameters and examples.
Structured success and failure results with applicable safety barriers.
alpha.summary: Available for real use and feedback while its interface and behavior can still evolve.

beta.label: Beta
promotion_requirements: Feature-complete behavior and maintained behavioral tests.
Real execution evidence for relevant environments.
Reviewed result contract with no known release-blocking defects.
beta.summary: Feature complete and broadly tested, with refinements and documented migrations still possible.

release_candidate.label: Release candidate
promotion_requirements: The intended Stable contract is frozen.
Final validation is limited to release-blocking defects.
release_candidate.summary: The command contract is frozen as a stable candidate while final validation looks for release-blocking defects.

stable.label: Stable
promotion_requirements: Release-candidate evidence remains valid across representative platforms.
Compatibility support and migration commitments are documented.
stable.summary: The documented command contract is supported for dependable use and compatibility changes follow a migration policy.

deprecated.label: Deprecated
promotion_requirements: A supported public replacement is identified.
Migration guidance and a support window are documented.
deprecated.summary: The command remains available during a documented migration period, with a supported replacement identified.

retired.label: Retired
promotion_requirements: Migration is complete and immutable release history preserves the former contract.
retired.summary: The command is no longer executable; historical release tags preserve its former contract and status.
